did: I landed the terminal card, after four review rounds that tightened how a card refuses a secret value. I built the cheat sheet, the stamp, the legend, the rule and the flow cards on branches that wait their turn. I rendered the NixOS upgrade and Rust scratchpad cheat-sheet videos twice each with the same bytes, and filed the badge timing bug I found on the way.

calls.title: Where a card's stamp sits, and whether a card can be drawn without one
options: At the foot of the card's body, and no card without one
In the frame's bottom corner, as the prototype had it
Only when the cut list has one
calls.why: The corner is where YouTube's controls and the captions go; the body's foot keeps the stamp inside the card's own space.
calls.undo: Make the stamp optional and give the card back its whole body.

calls.title: How the rule card writes its algebra
options: Draw the ∩ and ⇒ signs as shapes
calls.why: You asked for visual algebra, and the fonts lack both signs.
calls.undo: Swap the two signs for the words and and so.

calls.title: How a cheat sheet's row fades in
calls.why: Fading the row as one layer drew a corner pixel differently on each recording, and the same bytes twice is the promise.
calls.undo: Fade the row as a layer again; the recorder test will then fail.

calls.title: Whether the two videos' cut lists live in the repo
options: Keep them out of the repo
calls.why: They hold nothing private, and anyone can render the same bytes from them.

left: The cheat sheet, the stamp, legend and rule, and the flow card wait as branches, each opening after the one before merges; each needs main merged in first.
The two cut lists are committed but not pushed: the push needs your own go-ahead, and the hand-off on the epic has both files in full.
The badge timing bug, number 2982, waits until after the flow card lands.
Home rendering a cards essay, CARDS7, is next after that, and no one has started it.
